Technology stocks were slightly higher, with shares of tech stocks in the S&P 500 gaining 0.1% in value. The the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index was rising 0.4% this afternoon.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(-) SuperCom ( SPCB ) down almost 1% Tuesday afternoon, giving back a more than 7% advance for the Israeli cyber-security technologies company that followed it saying it won a new project from the government of an unidentified European country to install its PureSecurity electronic monitoring suite for use in house-arrest cases.
In other sector news:
(-) United Technologies ( UTX ) was slipping about 5% on Tuesday after confirming plans to split into the three independent companies as the company completed its $30 billion acquisition of Rockwell Collins. Moving ahead, the combination of Collins Aerospace Systems and UTX's defense and aerospace business will continue under the United Tech name while the new Pratt & Whitney, Otis, company will produce elevators and moving walkways. The third separate business, Carrier, will make heating, ventilation and air conditioning materials along with refrigeration and building automation products. The three-way split is expected to be completed in 2020.
(-) Apple ( AAPL ) was down almost 1% in Tuesday trading. RBC Capital Markets lowered its price target on the tech giant and President Donald Trump said late on Monday the previously exempt Apple products could be subject to tariffs should the forthcoming trade talks with China at the G20 summit in Argentina fail to go his way.
